Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {2}
Produces: Near-infinite +1/+1 counters on a creature; Put all creature cards from your library onto the battlefield tapped; Near-infinite creature ETB; Near-infinite creature LTB; Near-infinite creature sacrifice triggers; Near-infinite death triggers
Start: Ghired, Mirror of the Wilds (battlefield); Atla Palani, Nest Tender (battlefield); Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter (battlefield); Samut, Tyrant Smasher (battlefield)
Steps: Activate Atla by paying {2} and tapping it, creating an 0/1 Egg creature token with defender.
  Activate a nontoken creature you control using the ability granted to it by Ghired by tapping it, creating a copy of the Egg token.
  Activate Vish Kal by sacrificing an Egg token.
  When the Egg dies, Atla triggers, causing you to reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a creature card and put it onto the battlefield.
  Resolve the Vish Kal ability, putting a number of +1/+1 counters on Vish Kal equal to the sacrificed creature's power
  Repeat from step 2.
Notes: Depending on how many counters this combo puts on Vish Kal, you can activate its last ability to kill some number of creatures.

Start: Havi, the All-Father (battlefield); Gerrard, Weatherlight Hero (battlefield); Viscera Seer (battlefield)
Steps: Activate Viscera Seer by sacrificing Gerrard.
  When Gerrard dies, it and Havi trigger.
  Resolve the Havi trigger, returning up to one legendary creature card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Holding priority, activate Viscera Seer by sacrificing Havi.
  When Havi dies, it triggers, returning Gerrard from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Resolve the Gerrard trigger from step 2, failing to exile it as it is no longer in your graveyard and returning Havi from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Resolve the Viscera Seer abilities from step 1 and 4.
  Repeat.

Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {2}
Produces: Near-infinite +1/+1 counters on a creature; Put all creature cards from your library onto the battlefield tapped; Near-infinite creature ETB; Near-infinite creature LTB; Near-infinite creature sacrifice triggers; Near-infinite death triggers
Start: Ghired, Mirror of the Wilds (battlefield); Atla Palani, Nest Tender (battlefield); Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter (battlefield); Lavaleaper (battlefield)
Steps: Activate Atla by paying {2} and tapping it, creating an 0/1 Egg creature token with defender.
  Activate a nontoken creature you control using the ability granted to it by Ghired by tapping it, creating a copy of the Egg token.
  Activate Vish Kal by sacrificing an Egg token.
  When the Egg dies, Atla triggers, causing you to reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a creature card and put it onto the battlefield.
  Resolve the Vish Kal ability, putting a number of +1/+1 counters on Vish Kal equal to the sacrificed creature's power
  Repeat from step 2.
Notes: Depending on how many counters this combo puts on Vish Kal, you can activate its last ability to kill some number of creatures.

Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {2}
Produces: Put all creature cards from your library onto the battlefield tapped; Near-infinite creature ETB; Near-infinite creature LTB; Near-infinite death triggers; Near-infinite creature sacrifice triggers; Near-infinite scry 1
Start: Ghired, Mirror of the Wilds (battlefield); Atla Palani, Nest Tender (battlefield); Viscera Seer (battlefield); Purphoros, Bronze-Blooded (battlefield)
Steps: Activate Atla by paying {2} and tapping it, creating an 0/1 Egg creature token with defender.
  Activate a nontoken creature you control using the ability granted to it by Ghired by tapping it, creating a copy of the Egg token.
  Activate Viscera Seer by sacrificing an Egg token.
  When the Egg dies, Atla triggers, causing you to reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a creature card and put it onto the battlefield.
  Resolve the Viscera Seer ability, causing you to scry 1
  Repeat from step 2.

## Combo 248-1916-6473
Cards: Changeling Berserker + Changeling Titan + Mardu Siegebreaker
Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 6 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {0} plus the mana cost of the creature in your hand
Produces: Infinite creature ETB; Infinite creature LTB
Start: Changeling Berserker (hand, battlefield, exile: Exiled by the creature on the battlefield); Changeling Titan (hand, battlefield, exile: Exiled by the creature on the battlefield); Mardu Siegebreaker (hand, battlefield, exile: Exiled by the creature on the battlefield)

Steps: Cast Changeling Berserker for its mana cost.
  When Changeling Berserker enters, it exiles Changeling Titan until Changeling Berserker leaves the battlefield. Resolve any additional effects of Changeling Berserker's ETB.

  When Changeling Berserker leaves the battlefield, Changeling Titan is returned from exile to the battlefield.
  When Changeling Titan enters, it exiles Mardu Siegebreaker until Changeling Titan leaves the battlefield. Resolve any additional effects of Changeling Titan's ETB.
  When Mardu Siegebreaker leaves the battlefield, Changeling Berserker is returned from exile to the battlefield.
  Repeat from step 2.
Notes: Due to differences in card templating between the various banisher effects (linked triggered abilities vs "until" clause), steps 3, 5, and 7 may return the creature to the battlefield during the resolution of the preceding step rather than creating a separate event. This should not affect the overall execution of the combo, only how many objects pass through the stack (and thus rounds of priority available per loop).

Produces: Near-infinite creature tokens; Near-infinite card draw; Infinite self-mill; Near-infinite creature ETB; Near-infinite landfall triggers; Near-infinite draw triggers; Near-infinite self-discard triggers
Start: The Gitrog Monster (battlefield); Kodama of the East Tree (battlefield); Dakmor Salvage (hand); Maja, Bretagard Protector (battlefield); Need for Speed (battlefield)
Prerequisites: You are able to play a land this turn.
Steps: Play Dakmor Salvage.
  When Dakmor Salvage enters, Maja and Kodama trigger.
  Resolve the Kodama trigger, choosing to put nothing onto the battlefield.
  Holding priority, activate Need for Speed by sacrificing Dakmor Salvage.
  The Gitrog Monster's second ability triggers, causing you to mill two cards and return Dakmor Salvage from your graveyard to your hand.
  If a land was milled this way, The Gitrog Monster's second ability triggers, causing you to draw a card.
  Resolve the Need for Speed ability
  Resolve the Maja trigger, creating a token.
  When the token enters the battlefield, Kodama triggers, putting Dakmor Salvage from your hand onto the battlefield.
  When Dakmor Salvage enters the battlefield, Maja triggers.
  Repeat from step 4.

  When Dakmor Salvage enters the battlefield, The Necrobloom triggers.
  Repeat from step 4.
  Proceed to your cleanup step, and discard a land and any other card(s) as needed down to your maximum hand size.
  The Gitrog Monster triggers, causing you to mill two cards and return a land from your graveyard to your hand.
  Repeat, as you will still be over your maximum hand size and will be required to discard again.

## Combo 404-1251-1521-2105
Cards: Ghired, Conclave Exile + Combat Celebrant + Flamerush Rider + Dragonlord Kolaghan
Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal
Produces: Infinite combat phases; Infinite copies of attacking creatures you control; Infinite mana creatures you control can produce; Infinite tapped creature tokens; Infinite death triggers; Infinite creature ETB; Infinite creature LTB; Infinite untap of creatures you control
Start: Ghired, Conclave Exile (battlefield); Combat Celebrant (battlefield); Flamerush Rider (battlefield); Dragonlord Kolaghan (battlefield)
Prerequisites: An opponent cannot block creatures you control.
Steps: Declare Flamerush Rider, Combat Celebrant and Ghired as attackers, choosing to exert Combat Celebrant as it attacks.
  Combat Celebrant, Ghired's second ability and Flamerush Rider trigger.
  Resolve the Flamerush Rider trigger, creating a token copy of Combat Celebrant that is tapped and attacking.
  Resolve the Ghired trigger, creating a copy of the Combat Celebrant token.
  Resolve the Combat Celebrant trigger, untapping all other creatures you control and causing you to get an additional combat phase after this one.
  Move to your next combat phase, and declare the Combat Celebrant token created in step 4 and Ghired as attackers, choosing to exert the Combat Celebrant token as it attacks.
  Repeat from step 4.
  Optionally, you may also attack with Flamerush Rider to get infinite copies of any other attacking creatures you control.

Start: Beifong's Bounty Hunters (battlefield); Dwarven Mine (battlefield); Vish Kal, Blood Arbiter (battlefield); Horizon Explorer (battlefield)
Prerequisites: You control another nonland creature.

  Activate Vish Kal by sacrificing Dwarven Mine.

  When Dwarven Mine enters, it triggers, creating a 1/1 Dwarf creature token.
  Resolve the Vish Kal ability, putting a number of +1/+1 counters on Vish Kal equal to the sacrificed creature's power
  Repeat.
Notes: Once Vish Kal has infinite +1/+1 counters, you may activate its last ability any number of times to reduce the toughnesses of any number of creatures to 0.

Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal
Produces: Infinite lifegain; Infinite lifeloss; Infinite lifegain triggers; Infinitely large creature until end of turn; Infinite +1/+1 counters on a creature; Infinite creature LTB; Infinite creature ETB; Infinite creature sacrifice triggers
Start: Ygra, Eater of All (battlefield); Cauldron Familiar (graveyard); Ravenous Intruder (battlefield); Quintorius, Field Historian (battlefield)
Prerequisites: You control another Food.
Steps: Activate Cauldron Familiar by sacrificing a Food.
  Ygra triggers, putting two +1/+1 counters on it.
  Resolve the Cauldron Familiar ability, returning it from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Cauldron Familiar and Quintorius trigger.
  Resolve the Quintorius trigger, creating a creature token.
  Resolve the Cauldron Familiar trigger, causing each opponent to lose 1 life and you to gain 1 life.
  Activate Ravenous Intruder by sacrificing Cauldron Familiar.
  When Cauldron Familiar dies, Ygra triggers, putting two +1/+1 counters on it.
  Resolve the Ravenous Intruder ability.
  Repeat.

Start: Peregrin Took (battlefield); Cauldron Familiar (battlefield); Spawning Pit (battlefield); Quintorius, History Chaser (battlefield)

Steps: Activate Spawning Pit's first ability by sacrificing Cauldron Familiar.

  Repeat

  When the lands enter, Emeria Shepherd triggers that many times.

  Resolve the Woe Strider ability.

Steps: Activate Secluded Steppe's cycling ability by paying {W} and discarding it.
   Surly Badgersaur's second ability triggers, creating a Treasure artifact token.
  Resolve the Secluded Steppe ability, causing you to mill three cards and return Life from the Loam from your graveyard to your hand.
  Activate Skirge Familiar by discarding a land card, adding {B}.
  Surly Badgersaur's second ability triggers, creating a Treasure artifact token.
  Repeat from step 4 one additional time.
  Activate two Treasure tokens by tapping and sacrificing them, adding {G}{W}.
  Cast Life from the Loam by paying {1}{G}, returning Secluded Steppe and two other lands from your graveyard to your hand.
  Repeat.

Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 89 | Commander: legal | Mana needed: {2}{B/R}{B/R}
Produces: Infinite creature LTB; Infinite creature ETB; Infinite death triggers
Start: Murderous Redcap (hand); Good-Fortune Unicorn (battlefield)
Steps: Cast Murderous Redcap by paying {2}{B/R}{B/R}.
  When Murderous Redcap enters the battlefield, it and Good-Fortune Unicorn trigger.
  Resolve the Good-Fortune Unicorn trigger, putting a +1/+1 counter on Murderous Redcap.
  Resolve the Murderous Redcap trigger, dealing an amount of damage to itself equal to its power.
  Murderous Redcap dies as a state-based action due to having 0 toughness.
  Murderous Redcap's persist ability triggers, returning it from your graveyard to the battlefield with a -1/-1 counter on it.
  Repeat from step 2.

## Combo 1669-3234-3293-6495
Cards: Emeria Shepherd + World Shaper + Evereth, Viceroy of Plunder + Thaumatog
Color identity: BRGW | Bracket: 1+ (Exhibition) | Popularity: 0 | Commander: legal
Produces: Infinite self-mill; Infinite damage; Infinite +1/+1 counters on a creature; Infinitely large creature until end of turn; Infinite creature ETB; Infinite creature LTB; Infinite creature sacrifice triggers; Infinite death triggers; Infinite landfall triggers; Return all nonland permanents from your graveyard to the battlefield
Start: Emeria Shepherd (battlefield); World Shaper (battlefield); Evereth, Viceroy of Plunder (battlefield); Thaumatog (battlefield)
Prerequisites: You control a Plains or have a Plains in your graveyard.
Steps: Activate Thaumatog by sacrificing a land.
  Repeat step 1 until you control no lands.
  Activate Evereth by sacrificing World Shaper.
  When World Shaper dies, it triggers, return all lands from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped.
  When the lands enter, Emeria Shepherd triggers that many times.
  Resolve an Emeria Shepherd trigger that was triggered by a Plains, returning World Shaper from your graveyard to the battlefield.
  Resolve all remaining Emeria Shepherd triggers.
  Resolve the Evereth ability.
  Repeat
Notes: You can return all nonland permanents in your graveyard and library to the battlefield if you control there are two or more Plains between your graveyard, library and battlefield. To do this, have all triggers from Emeria Shepherd target desired permanents. Then, resolve the Plains triggers first to return those cards to the battlefield, causing all other triggers to fizzle on the stack.
  If you have a way to kill Evereth and {1}{B/R} available, you can do so after putting a significant amount of +1/+1 counters on it to deal damage to each opponent using its second ability.
